title: Presence matrix
rule: Strong: at least one card from that people in that chapter is a verbatim quotation sharing two or more of the chapter's motifs, or any card sharing three or more. Weak: the people has a card there, but only a paraphrase or a single shared motif. Empty: this book holds no card from that people on that motif — which says nothing about what that people has or has not preserved.

routes.same-world: Same world as the Hebrew record — the Near East; contact is constant.
routes.route: A documented route to the Near East (trade, conquest, script or religion) existed before the text was written down.
routes.late: A route existed only late: the text was written down after Christian or Islamic contact, so transmission is possible and has to be weighed.
routes.none: No route to the Near East is known before European contact; the text was written down after that contact, by or through outsiders.
routes.catalogue: A comparative catalogue, not a people.

cultures.name: Hebrew
cultures.routeNote: The Hebrew record itself.

cultures.name: Babylon & Assyria
cultures.routeNote: Mesopotamia; Judah's neighbour and, in the end, its captor.

cultures.name: Greek
cultures.routeNote: Aegean trade with the Levant from the Bronze Age; the Greek alphabet itself came from Phoenicia in the 8th century BCE.

cultures.name: Historians & sages
cultures.routeNote: Josephus, Eusebius and the other late compilers who quote earlier Near Eastern writers.

cultures.name: India
cultures.routeNote: Indus–Mesopotamia trade is documented c. 2500–1900 BCE (Indus seals and carnelian at Ur); Persia ruled the Indus from the 6th century BCE.

cultures.name: Sumer
cultures.routeNote: Southern Mesopotamia; the oldest written record in the book.

cultures.name: Dead Sea Scrolls
cultures.routeNote: Qumran, Judea; Hebrew and Aramaic scrolls of the Second Temple period.

cultures.name: Egypt
cultures.routeNote: The Nile; Canaan's neighbour and often its overlord.

cultures.name: China
cultures.routeNote: The Silk Road is documented from the 2nd century BCE; the earliest Chinese texts here predate it, and no earlier route to the Near East is documented.

cultures.name: Norse
cultures.routeNote: The Eddas were written down in 13th-century Christian Iceland; Norse traders had reached Byzantium and Baghdad from the 9th century.

cultures.name: Persia
cultures.routeNote: Ruled Judah from 539 BCE; the Hebrew record's own empire for two centuries.

cultures.name: Aztec
cultures.routeNote: No route before 1519; the surviving accounts were written down under Spanish rule.

cultures.name: Many peoples
cultures.routeNote: A comparative catalogue of traditions, not a people.

cultures.name: Canaan / Ugarit
cultures.routeNote: The land itself; the Ugarit tablets are the Hebrew record's nearest neighbour.

cultures.name: Hawaii
cultures.routeNote: No route before 1778; the Kumulipo was written down in the 19th century.

cultures.name: Andean / Inca
cultures.routeNote: No route before 1532; recorded by Spanish-era chroniclers.

cultures.name: Arabia
cultures.routeNote: Israel's neighbour and trading partner throughout; the Qur'an stands inside the same scriptural world.

cultures.name: Assyria
cultures.routeNote: The empire that took Samaria.

cultures.name: Maasai
cultures.routeNote: East Africa; the Swahili coast was in Indian Ocean trade from the 1st millennium CE; recorded in the early 20th century.

cultures.name: Maya
cultures.routeNote: No route before 1492; the Popol Vuh was written down in the 1550s, after the conquest.

cultures.name: The Celts
cultures.routeNote: Irish and Welsh traditions were written down by medieval Christian scribes.

cultures.name: The Slavs
cultures.routeNote: Written down after Byzantine Christianization, from the 10th century on.

cultures.name: Aboriginal
cultures.routeNote: No route before 1788; recorded in the 19th and 20th centuries.

cultures.name: Across traditions
cultures.routeNote: A comparative catalogue of traditions, not a people.

cultures.name: Anishinaabe
cultures.routeNote: No route before European contact; recorded in the 19th century.

cultures.name: Aram (Damascus)
cultures.routeNote: Damascus and its kings; the Tel Dan stele.

cultures.name: Choctaw
cultures.routeNote: No route before European contact; recorded in the 19th and 20th centuries.

cultures.name: Comanche
cultures.routeNote: No route before European contact; recorded in the 20th century.

cultures.name: Ethiopia
cultures.routeNote: Red Sea trade with South Arabia and Egypt is ancient; the Kebra Nagast itself was written in the 14th century in a Christian kingdom.

cultures.name: Finland & Karelia
cultures.routeNote: The Kalevala was compiled from oral runes in 1835–49, in Christian Finland.

cultures.name: Inuit
cultures.routeNote: Norse settlers reached Greenland c. 1000 CE, but no Near Eastern route is known; recorded in the 19th and 20th centuries.

cultures.name: Japan
cultures.routeNote: Chinese script and Buddhism reached Japan in the 6th century CE and the Kojiki was written in 712; no direct Near Eastern route is known.

cultures.name: Moab
cultures.routeNote: Israel's neighbour across the Jordan; the Mesha Stele names Israel.

cultures.name: Navajo
cultures.routeNote: No route before European contact; recorded in the 19th and 20th centuries.

cultures.name: Paiute
cultures.routeNote: No route before European contact; the account here was written by a Paiute author in 1883.

cultures.name: Tyre (Phoenicia)
cultures.routeNote: Tyre and Sidon; Solomon's partners in the text and in Josephus's Tyrian annals.

cultures.name: Yoruba
cultures.routeNote: West Africa; trans-Saharan and Islamic contact from the 11th century; recorded in the 19th and 20th centuries.
